evidence_wording: A statistical classification of diseases must be confined to a limited number of mutually exclusive categories able to encompass the complete range of morbid conditions. ... The following measures apply in determining whether an entity qualifies to become a unique category: 1. Epidemiological evidence ... 2. Clinical evidence ... 3. Granularity ... 4. Continuity ... 5. Parsimony: the need to limit the number of categories for international mandatory reporting.

title: Content model and definition of disease
subject: disease (ICD-11 content model)
object: a set of dysfunctions in any body system defined by symptomatology/manifestations, aetiology, course and outcome, treatment response, linkage to genetic factors, linkage to environmental factors
context: for further information on the content model see 3.4 The Content Model
evidence_wording: A disease is usually defined using a set of relevant aspects drawn from the pattern below. A disease is a set of dysfunctions in any body system defined by: [table of properties: Symptomatology or manifestations; Aetiology; Course and outcome; Treatment response; Linkage to genetic factors; Linkage to environmental factors].

title: ICD Chapter structure
subject: ICD chapter structure ('special groups' chapters)
predicate: take priority over 'body systems' chapters when
object: there is any doubt as to where a condition should be positioned; enforced in the 'excludes' notes at the beginning of each chapter
context: ICD is a variable-axis classification derived from William Farr's structure; in general, conditions are primarily classified to one of the 'special groups' chapters
evidence_wording: Where there is any doubt as to where a condition should be positioned, the ‘special groups’ chapters take priority. This principle is enforced in the ‘excludes’ notes at the beginning of each chapter in the ICD.

title: Guiding principles for classification of special concepts
subject: placement of special concepts in ICD-11
object: clinical findings in Chapter 21; clinical manifestations in body system chapter (underlying condition has to be coded as well); syndromes of unknown aetiology with most relevant body system; 'due to' / 'multiple' / 'sequelae' / 'history of' categories restricted to exceptions; residual categories exist only where meaningful
context: acute postprocedural complications identified by combinations of codes from body system or injury chapters and external causes chapter
exception_condition: categories with mention of 'multiple' require coding of the different multiple conditions individually; 'sequelae' include residual effects specified as arrested, cured, healed, inactive, old or quiescent unless there is evidence of active disease
evidence_wording: The number of categories with ‘due to’ in the title are restricted to certain exceptions. ... Categories with mention of ‘multiple’ are restricted to exceptions and require coding of the different multiple conditions individually (e.g. multiple injuries are to be coded individually when possible). ... Residual categories exist only where they are meaningful.

title: General features of ICD-11 / Code structure
subject: ICD-11 stem codes
object: the range from 1A00.00 to ZZ9Z.ZZ; first character relates to the chapter number; a letter always in second position; letters O and I omitted; terminal Y reserved for 'other specified', terminal Z for 'unspecified' ('F'/'G' also used in chapters with more than 240 blocks)
context: main structural innovation: built on a Foundation Component from which Tabular lists are derived; codes starting with 'X' indicate an extension code (see 2.9); a dash in the Reference Guide indicates more detailed codes exist, e.g. 8B24- covers 8B24.0 to 8B24.Z
evidence_wording: The codes of the ICD–11 are alphanumeric and cover the range from 1A00.00 to ZZ9Z.ZZ. ... The letters ‘O’ and ‘I’ are omitted to prevent confusion with the numbers ‘0’ and ‘1’. ... The terminal letter Y is reserved for the residual category ‘other specified’ and the terminal letter ‘Z’ is reserved for the residual category ‘unspecified’.

title: Uniform resource identifiers
subject: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI)
object: a string of characters that uniquely identifies a particular ICD-11 entity; each entity has a specific place in the hierarchy of groups and categories
evidence_wording: All entities have a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) which is a string of characters that uniquely identifies a particular ICD-11 entity. Each entity has a specific place in the hierarchy of groups and categories.

title: Block codes
subject: ICD-11 blocks
object: reporting aggregated statistics; blocks do not have category codes as they are not supposed to be used in coding
context: blocks have their own URIs (e.g. Neoplasms http://id.who.int/icd/entity/1630407678) and block IDs 11 characters long (e.g. 'BlockL1-1A0')
exception_condition: blocks are not supposed to be used in coding
evidence_wording: Higher level entities in ICD-11 (called ‘blocks’) may be used for reporting aggregated statistics. However, blocks do not have category codes as they are not supposed to be used in coding. Blocks have their own URIs (e.g. the URI for Neoplasms is http://id.who.int/icd/entity/1630407678).

title: Stem codes
subject: stem codes
object: codes in the Tabular list of ICD-11 that can be used alone; designed to ensure meaningful information in use cases that require only one code per case
context: stem codes may be entities or groupings of high relevance in any of the use cases, or clinical conditions that should always be described as one single category
evidence_wording: Codes in the Tabular list of ICD-11 that can be used alone. Stem codes may be entities or groupings of high relevance in any of the use cases, or clinical conditions that should always be described as one single category. Stem codes are designed to ensure that in use cases that require only one code per case, meaningful information is collected.

title: Extension codes and postcoordination
subject: extension codes
predicate: are not to be used alone in the context of statistical classification but
object: must be added to a stem code; postcoordination links core diagnostic concepts (stem+stem) and/or extension codes into a cluster; permitted with all axes as long as at least one stem code is used
context: postcoordination is one of the significant changes compared with ICD-10; API, Browser and coding tool facilitate postcoordination in certain areas; refer to 2.9
exception_condition: extension codes may be used in another context, e.g. for device documentation; not all extension codes can be used with every stem code
evidence_wording: Extension codes are not to be used alone in the context of statistical classification but must be added to a stem code. ... Postcoordination is by matter of principle permitted with all axes, as long as at least one stem code is used.

title: Other general features
subject: ICD-11 category descriptions and special tabulation lists
object: short descriptions (maximum 100 words) in the Tabular list plus long 'additional information' descriptions without length restriction; special tabulation lists plus SMoL, verbal autopsy list, and infectious diseases by agent list
context: special tabulation lists refer to section 2.25; specialty linearisations allow representation of content from a specialty perspective
evidence_wording: ICD–11 categories have short descriptions, plus long descriptions labelled ‘additional information’. The short description is a maximum of 100 words ... Special tabulation lists (refer to section 2.25) continue to exist in ICD-11, but there are three additional lists - the Startup Mortality List (SMoL), the list for verbal autopsy, and the list for infectious diseases by agent.

title: Foundation Component and Tabular lists of ICD-11
subject: ICD-11 Foundation Component
object: a multidimensional collection of all ICD entities; an underlying database that holds all necessary information to generate print versions of the tabular list and the alphabetical index, specialty linearisations and country-specific modifications
context: in a Tabular list, entities become categories that are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive, linked to a mono hierarchical tree (only one parent); multiple-parent information remains available from the Foundation Component; several congruent tabular lists can be built from the same Foundation Component
evidence_wording: The Foundation Component is a multidimensional collection of all ICD entities. ... In a Tabular list, entities of the Foundation Component become categories. The categories are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive and linked to a mono hierarchical tree (that is, they have only one parent).

title: Precoordination and Postcoordination in ICD-11
subject: precoordination and postcoordination
object: precoordination: stem codes contain all pertinent information in a pre-combined fashion; postcoordination: combining multiple codes (two or more stem codes e.g. code1/code2, or stem code&extension code1&extension code2); the combination is called a cluster (refer to 2.10)
evidence_wording: A health condition may be described to any level of detail, by applying more than one code, or by ‘postcoordinating’ (i.e. combining): two or more stem codes, (e.g. code1/code2); stem codes with one or more extension codes. (e.g. stem code&extension code1&extension code2). ... The combination of codes is called a cluster. Refer to 2.10.

title: Multiple parenting
subject: multiple parenting
object: an entity to be correctly classified in two different places (e.g. by site or by aetiology); the decision about which place depends on international agreement and legacy
context: examples: oesophageal cancer (neoplasms vs digestive system); cerebral ischaemic conditions (vascular vs nervous system)
evidence_wording: An entity may be correctly classified in two different places, e.g. by site or by aetiology. For a disease, such as oesophageal cancer, this would mean that it could be classified to cancers (malignant neoplasms) or to conditions of the digestive system. ... A decision about which place a condition is in depends on international agreement and legacy.

title: Language independent ICD entities
subject: ICD-11 entities
object: language independent; the content model allows binding of any desired language to the elements of its Foundation Component
context: international maintenance handled in English; international translation base facilitates translations or multilingual browsing (See 3.12 Annex A)
evidence_wording: ICD-11 entities are language independent. The maintenance of the ICD-11 on an international level is handled in the English language but the content model of ICD–11 is language independent and allows binding of any desired language to the elements of its Foundation Component.

title: Main uses of the ICD: Mortality
subject: mortality statistics
object: medical research, monitoring of public health, evaluating health interventions, and planning and follow-up of health care; WHA rules standardise selection of a single cause for routine tabulation
context: implementation of the ICD for mortality requires infrastructure for reporting and storing information, design of information flows, quality assurance and feedback, and training
evidence_wording: Rules adopted by the World Health Assembly (WHA) regarding the selection of a single cause or condition, from death certificates, for routine tabulation of mortality statistics are provided to standardise production of mortality data.

title: What is coded: Causes of death
subject: underlying cause of death
object: (a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced the fatal injury
context: selected for routine single-cause tabulation of mortality statistics; effective public health interventions prevent harm or death by breaking the chain of events that lead to harm (See Section 2.21)
evidence_wording: the underlying cause of death has been defined as “(a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced the fatal injury”, and is selected for routine single-cause tabulation of mortality statistics.

title: Main uses of the ICD: Morbidity
subject: morbidity data
object: statistical reporting mostly at national or local levels; basis for casemix systems such as Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs); inform clinical guidelines through Foundation Component information on burden of disease
evidence_wording: Morbidity data are used for statistical reporting mostly at national or local levels. ... ICD coded data also forms the basis for different casemix systems, such as different varieties of Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs).

title: What is coded: patient conditions
subject: main condition
object: the one condition determined to be the reason for admission, established at the end of the episode of health care; the health care practitioner should record and identify it
context: the definition of main condition relates to the description of an episode of hospital-based care; the practitioner responsible for treatment is responsible for documenting conditions; clinical documentation is the starting point for coded health data (See Section 1.4)
evidence_wording: The health care practitioner should record and identify as the main condition the one condition that is determined to be the reason for admission, established at the end of the episode of health care. ... The importance of clinical documentation by health care practitioners as the starting point for coded health data cannot be overstated, and needs to be underlined as being a matter of key significance within countries and internationally.

title: Traditional Medicine
subject: Traditional Medicine (TM) chapter (TM1)
object: in conjunction with the Western Medicine concepts of ICD Chapters 1-25
context: international standardisation allows measuring, counting, comparing and monitoring over time; see 3.12 Annex A: ICD-11 Updating and Maintenance
exception_condition: the TM1 chapter is not designed to assess TM practice or the efficacy of any TM intervention
evidence_wording: It is recommended that coding of cases with ICD-11’s chapter on Traditional Medicine disorders and patterns (TM1) be used in conjunction with the Western Medicine concepts of ICD Chapters 1-25. As with other ICD chapters, the TM1 chapter is not designed to assess TM practice or the efficacy of any TM intervention.

title: ICD maintenance
subject: ICD maintenance process
object: updating of the ICD following evolution in understanding of diseases, treatments, and prevention; standardised open proposal and review mechanism on an online platform
context: workflows ensure proposed changes are considered from a medical and scientific perspective and from their value and place in a particular use case (See 3.12 Annex A)
evidence_wording: A standardised open process has been established to ensure that the proposed updates are collected, routed, reviewed, and duly considered before being implemented. A proposal and review mechanism on an online platform makes the process transparent.

title: Guiding principles of authoring process
subject: allocation of entities in the classification
predicate: follows rules in order of priority:
object: 1. no changes without rationale and documented change in aetiology or prevention method; 2. conditions classified predominantly by their aetiology; 3. conditions that could arguably be in two or more places remain in their legacy location; 4. keeping a group of subtypes together may override anatomical or aetiological considerations
context: e.g. Chapter 04 'Diseases of the immune system' added on sufficient scientific evidence; viral hepatitis in 'Certain infectious or parasitic disease'; human prion diseases kept together despite mixed components
exception_condition: where one condition can be due to multiple different aetiologies, and it is more relevant to retain the affected body system, it is usually classified with the body system
evidence_wording: No changes to the classification, including movement of categories or groups between chapters, without rationale and documented change in aetiology or prevention method. ... Conditions are classified predominantly by their aetiology. ... Conditions that could arguably be in two or more places of the classification remain in their legacy location. ... Keeping a group of subtypes together in one location may override anatomical or aetiological considerations.

title: Improving user guidance
subject: user guidance rules
object: add secondary parents where a condition could be in two or more places (creating a window with no primary children/terms/residual categories if needed); add an exclusion note for confusable conditions; create special linearisation lists for alternative tabulation; allow specialty linearisations (primary care, dermatology, neurology, ophthalmology, ICD-O, ICECI)
context: multiple parenting in the Foundation Component serves to address users expecting to find conditions in certain places; deprecated terms hidden from the ICD-11 browser (tabular) and not under 'All Index Terms'
evidence_wording: Where a condition could be in two or more places, identify these other places and add them as secondary parents ... Where a condition could be confused with another condition bearing a similar name, add an exclusion note. (e.g. ‘Influenza due to seasonal influenza virus’ has a note ‘Exclusion: Haemophilus influenzae [H. influenzae] meningitis’). ... Deprecated term: A term/concept that has been deemed invalid (outdated) for inclusion in the current version of ICD-11, which may still be recorded.

title: Introduction to the ICD-11 Update Process
subject: ICD-11 update process
predicate: is carried out at different levels with different frequencies:
object: continuous updates to Foundation Component and index entries; annual official releases ('blue browser'); every five years for updates impacting four- and five-character codes; every ten years for mortality and morbidity rules with significant statistical impact
context: any individual user can submit a proposal for an update; maintenance platform ('orange browser') used for proposals and comments; input requires proper referencing of sources, scientific evidence, and copyright permission
temporal_qualifier: annually / every five years / every ten years
evidence_wording: Continuous updates are made to the: ICD-11 Foundation Component; ICD-11 index entries. Official releases of the ICD-11 classification are produced: - Annually for international use in mortality and morbidity (known as the ‘blue browser’). Every five years for updates that impact on the four- and five-character codes. Every ten years for updates to the mortality and morbidity rules that have significant impact on statistical output.

title: National Modifications for morbidity coding
subject: national modifications of ICD-11
object: ideally agreed by ICD-11 maintenance bodies before national implementation; should not impact morbidity and mortality statistics and should not conflict with the foundation; approval subject to whether suitable detail already exists in the foundation; must incorporate changes to the international version as soon as possible; contractual arrangements with WHO required
context: example: 'Diabetes Type 1' is classified to 5A10 in the WHO version; a national modification could add 5A10.1 'Diabetes Type 1, uncontrolled', but when postcoordination provides the necessary detail a new subcategory may not be necessary
exception_condition: when the mechanism of postcoordination provides the necessary detail, the addition of a new subcategory may not be necessary
evidence_wording: All countries planning to produce national modifications must make relevant contractual arrangements with WHO. ... Modifications should not impact on morbidity and mortality statistics, and should not conflict with the foundation. ... If a change is made to the international version of ICD-11 the respective national modification must incorporate the change as soon as possible.

title: Part 2 - Using ICD-11 / Basic coding and reporting guidelines
subject: coding
object: the assignment of one or more codes in order to represent the meaning of a condition in as much detail as required
context: recommended to use the ICD-11 Smart coding tool (online and offline); print version option not recommended (time consuming, may cause confusion); if no electronic environment available, solutions in collaboration with WHO
exception_condition: Software must not include lists or other prompts to guide the recording or coding, as these necessarily limit the range of diagnoses and therefore have an adverse effect on the accuracy and usefulness of the record and report.
evidence_wording: Coding is the assignment of one or more codes in order to represent the meaning of a condition in as much detail as required. ... Software must not include lists or other prompts to guide the recording or coding, as these necessarily limit the range of diagnoses and therefore have an adverse effect on the accuracy and usefulness of the record and report.

title: Tabular List, Special Tabulation Lists, Qualifiers, and Modifiers
subject: ICD-11 Tabular list
object: an alphanumeric listing of diseases and disease groups, inclusion and exclusion notes, and some coding rules; Chapters 1 to 25 contain approximately 15 000 entities at the four-, five- or six-character level
context: special tabulation lists presented at the end of the Tabular list; not designed for coding but for tabulation and reporting only (2.25); extension codes (2.9) and Traditional medicine (1.5) sections exist in addition
exception_condition: Special tabulation lists are not designed for coding but are for tabulation and reporting only
evidence_wording: The Tabular list is an alphanumeric listing of diseases and disease groups, inclusion and exclusion notes, and some coding rules. Chapters 1 to 25 of the ICD contain approximately 15 000 entities at the four-, five- or six-character level. ... Special tabulation lists are not designed for coding but are for tabulation and reporting only (2.25).

title: Index
subject: ICD-11 Alphabetical Index
object: a list of more than 120 000 clinical terms (including synonyms or phrases) used to find the relevant ICD codes or code combinations
exception_condition: mention of a term in the index exclusively serves coding; it does not mean approval or endorsement of a particular condition
evidence_wording: The Alphabetical Index is a list of more than 120 000 clinical terms (including synonyms or phrases). The index is used to find the relevant ICD codes or code combinations for clinical terms. The mention of a term in the index exclusively serves coding. Mention of a term in the index does not mean approval or endorsement of a particular condition.

title: Reference Guide
subject: ICD-11 Reference Guide
object: an introduction to the context, components, and intended [uses] (text continues into next segment, printed 49)
context: unit starts at bottom of printed 48 and continues in segment seg-0051-0075 (printed 49); hosted here per start-page rule
evidence_wording: The Reference Guide contains an introduction to the context, components, and intended

title: Coding step by step - electronic versus paper environment
subject: Coding procedure (electronic and paper)
object: entering or searching clinical terms, selecting matching terms, and verifying against exclusions, inclusions and notes
context: Section 2.6 step comparison table (electronic coding tool vs paper tabular list)
evidence_wording: Electronic: 1. Enter the statement or term in the coding tool; 2. Select the matching term, or the one closest to what you are looking for from amongst the displayed options; 3. Verify the result in the tabular list browser view for exclusions, inclusions and notes given at the level of that category, its grouping levels and at the chapter level. Paper: 1. Look up the lead term in the Alphabetical Index and applicable secondary terms; 2. Select the appropriate term, or one closest to what you are looking for, from amongst the listed options; 3. Verify the result in the tabular list (Volume 1) for exclusions, inclusions and notes given at the level of that category, its grouping levels and at the chapter level.

title: ICD-11 conventions - Inclusions
subject: Inclusion terms in ICD-11
object: non-exhaustive examples and synonyms of diagnostic statements classified to a category to delineate content and boundaries
context: Section 2.7 ICD-11 conventions and 2.7.1 Inclusions
evidence_wording: Within the coded categories there are typically other optional diagnostic terms. These are known as 'inclusion terms' and are given, in addition to the title, as examples of the diagnostic statements to be classified to that category. They may refer to different conditions or be synonyms. They are not a sub-classification of the category. Inclusion terms are listed primarily as a guide to the content of the category, in addition to the descriptions.

title: ICD-11 conventions - Exclusions and Multiple parenting
subject: Exclusion notes and multiple parenting
object: the boundaries of categories by directing coders to conditions classified elsewhere
context: Section 2.7.2 Exclusions and relationship to multiple parenting ('code elsewhere')
evidence_wording: Exclusions serve as a cross reference in ICD and help to delineate the boundaries of a category. General exclusions for a range of categories or for all subcategories are found in the notes heading 'Excludes', immediately following a chapter, group or category title. Multiple parenting in ICD-11 shows categories in the context of siblings that are placed elsewhere in the classification. This is also an indication of an exclusion and means 'a sibling is coded elsewhere'. In the print and the electronic version this is marked with the label 'code elsewhere'.

title: Code also and Use additional code instructions
subject: 'Code also' and 'Use additional code, if desired' instructions
object: mandatory aetiological cluster coding versus optional additional clinical detail
context: Section 2.7.2.1 instructions on cluster coding requirements
evidence_wording: 'Code also' instructions inform the user about required additional aetiological information which is mandatory to be coded in a cluster with certain categories because that additional information is relevant for primary tabulation. The 'code also' statement marks the categories that must be used in conjunction with the indicated second code(s). ... 'Use additional code, if desired' - instructions inform the user about optional additional detail that can be coded.

title: ICD-11 conventions - NEC (Not Elsewhere Classified) and NOS (Not Otherwise Specified)
subject: NEC and NOS abbreviations
object: specified variants categorized elsewhere in the system versus unspecified or incompletely documented conditions
context: Section 2.7.3, 2.7.3.1 NEC, and 2.7.3.2 NOS conventions
evidence_wording: The stem 'not elsewhere classified', when used in a category title, serve as a warning that certain specified variants of the listed conditions may appear in other parts of the classification. ... The letters NOS are an abbreviation for the term 'not otherwise specified', implying that the documentation that is used for classifying does not provide more detail beyond the term provided. It implies 'unspecified', 'incompletely specified' or 'unqualified'.

title: ICD-11 conventions - Certain, Residual categories (Other and Unspecified), and Logical operators
subject: Conventions for 'Certain', residual categories ('Other' and 'Unspecified'), and 'And' / 'Or'
object: semantic groupings, boundary handling for missing or unclassified conditions, and formal logic application
evidence_wording: The term 'certain' is used where certain entities that could be grouped in a specific location in the classification are grouped somewhere else outside the current chapter or block. ... In some instances, necessary information to select a specific category may not be available in the source documentation. When this is the case, the residual category 'unspecified' is selected. Conversely, there are instances where the information in the source documentation is very specific, but the tabular list does not include a specific category. In this case, users identify the closest category match, and code to the residual category titled 'other'. The words 'and' and 'or' in ICD-11 are used in their meaning in formal logic.

title: ICD-11 conventions - Relational phrases, spelling, grammar and typography
subject: Relational phrasing and editorial conventions in ICD-11
object: causal sequence distinction ('Due to' vs 'Associated with'), singular terms, omission of eponym apostrophes, and British/WHO spelling rules
context: Sections 2.7.7 and 2.7.8
evidence_wording: 'Due to' is the preferred term for categories where two conditions are mentioned, and a causal sequence exists between them. Other terms, such as 'caused by' or 'attributed to' are allowable synonyms. The phrase 'secondary to' is equivalent and may also be included as a synonym. 'Associated with' is the preferred term for categories where two conditions are mentioned but there is no causal sequence implied. Spelling and grammar of ICD-11 follow the British rules with exceptions and amendments conforming to WHO spelling rules. ... Terms are listed in their singular form. ... No use of apostrophes with eponyms. ... Entities are described using natural language.

title: Table 1 - ICD-11 Terminology (General features)
subject: ICD-11 core structural terminology
object: Foundation component, stem codes, extension codes, precoordination, postcoordination, cluster, and primary/secondary parents
context: Section 2.7.9 General features and Table 1: ICD-11 Terminology
evidence_wording: The main structural innovation of ICD-11 is that it is built on a Foundation component from which the tabular lists (such as the classification for morbidity and mortality statistics) is derived. Table 1 defines: Foundation component, Stem code, Extension code, Precoordination, Postcoordination, Cluster, Primary and secondary parents.

title: ICD-11 stem codes
subject: ICD-11 stem codes
object: standalone codes organized in 26 chapters designed to collect a meaningful minimum of information per case
context: Section 2.8 Stem codes definition and chapter organization
evidence_wording: ICD-11 stem codes are codes in a particular tabular list that can be used alone. Stem codes may be entities or groupings of high relevance, or clinical entities that should always be described as one entity. The design of stem codes makes sure that in use cases that require only one code per case a meaningful minimum of information is collected. The stem codes of the ICD-11 are organised in 26 chapters that follow the traditional pattern of the ICD, relating to aetiology, relevant organ system, maternal status, perinatal status, external causes, and factors influencing health status.

title: ICD-11 extension codes - Type 1 and Type 2
subject: Extension codes in ICD-11
object: supplementary multi-dimensional detail linked to stem codes, divided into Type 1 (detail/qualification) and Type 2 (diagnosis code descriptors)
context: Section 2.9 Extension codes definition, constraints, and overview
evidence_wording: Extension codes are provided for use as supplementary or additional codes when it is desired to identify more detail in classification entities elsewhere. ... Extension codes are not mutually exclusive. They are not a classification and can never be used without a stem code for statistical purposes. Extension codes can never appear in the first position in a classification cluster. There are two main types: Type 1 extension codes allow the user to add detail to a stem code in terms of severity, temporality, anatomy, histopathology... Type 2 extension codes represent diagnosis code descriptors which indicate how the diagnosis is to be used and/or interpreted (e.g. diagnosis timing XY6M present on admission).

title: Precoordination and postcoordination concepts and axes
subject: Precoordination and postcoordination mechanisms
object: combining stem codes and extension codes into clusters using specific relational axes (Has causing condition, Has manifestation, Associated with)
context: Section 2.10 Precoordination and postcoordination description and axes table
evidence_wording: Some stem codes contain all pertinent information about a clinical concept in a pre-combined fashion. This is referred to as 'precoordination'. A health condition may be further described to any level of detail, by applying more than one code, or by 'postcoordinating' (i.e. combining codes): two or more stem codes (code1/code2), stem codes with one or more extension codes (stem&ext). Postcoordination axes include: 'Has causing condition' (mandatory postcoordination, equivalent to ICD-10 dagger), 'Has manifestation' (optional postcoordination, equivalent to ICD-10 asterisk), and 'Associated with'.

title: Postcoordination rules and prohibition against duplicating precoordinated concepts
subject: Postcoordination clustering rules
object: existing precoordinated MMS stem codes must always be used and never duplicated or replicated via postcoordination
context: Section 2.10.1 Adding detail - cluster coding and strict prohibition
evidence_wording: Information about the aetiology and the manifestation of the condition of interest should be coded. ... Note: When a condition is already precoordinated and given an ICD-11 MMS code, the existing precoordinated ICD-11 MMS stem code must be used. Postcoordination must never be used to replicate the meaning of a precoordinated code. Also note that all ICD entities in the Foundation have a uniform resource identifier (URI). If a particular entity does not have an ICD-11 MMS code, and collection of a more detailed/specific entity is required for selected national needs, a country may collect the URI for this purpose.

title: Cluster coding syntax and ordering rules in complex clusters
subject: ICD-11 cluster syntax rules
object: separator usage (slash '/' between stem codes, ampersand '&' before extension codes) and use-case-specific ordering for mortality and morbidity
context: Section 2.10.2 Rules 1 to 5 for combining stem and extension codes in clusters
evidence_wording: Cluster coding requires use of a specific syntax to indicate which codes belong together when postcoordination is used: 1. If only one stem code is coded, no clustering mechanisms need to be observed. 2. Stem codes are always coded before extension codes. 3. If one stem code is postcoordinated with extension codes, the combining syntax used is the ampersand (&). 4. If two stem codes are postcoordinated, the first stem code is separated from the second by a slash (/); in mortality, priority is given to the code best describing aetiology; in morbidity, priority is given to the main condition. 5. If stem codes have extension codes, the first stem code and its extension codes (&) precede the slash (/), followed by the second stem code and its extension codes (&).

title: Diagnosis Timing extension codes - Present on admission vs Developed after admission
subject: Diagnosis timing extension codes (XY6M, XY69)
object: pre-existing conditions from hospital-acquired conditions and adverse events in inpatient morbidity reporting
context: Section 2.10.3 Diagnosis timing rules and hospital complication coding examples
evidence_wording: Among the new Type 2 Extension codes - Diagnosis Code Descriptors, diagnosis timing is the particularly important set of extension codes that allow for distinction of diagnoses present on admission from diagnoses arising after admission, i.e. during the period of hospitalisation. The latter distinction is particularly important, because it allows for the targeted identification of a number of in-hospital diagnoses that may represent adverse events associated with health care. ... The main condition does not need to be coded as present on admission because it is designated as the reason for admission.

title: ICD-11 Functioning section - ICF alignment and use cases
subject: ICD-11 Functioning section
object: operational tools for assessing and coding functioning aligned with ICF across clinical, administrative, and disability evaluation use cases
context: Section 2.11 Functioning section overview
evidence_wording: The Functioning section of ICD-11 allows coding and assessment of functioning in line with ICF but at an operational level. For detailed recording and assessment, the full ICF should be used. This section's concepts are aligned with ICF and allow an easy transition to ICF. The design of the functioning section in ICD-11 addresses documentation and assessment of the level of functioning of persons, for: general medical practice, work incapacity assessment, social benefits as for disability, payment or reimbursement, needs assessment in rehabilitation, and outcome evaluation.

title: WHODAS 2.0 features, domains, and IRT scoring algorithm
subject: WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0)
object: functioning and disability across 6 domains using Item Response Theory (IRT) metric converted from 0 to 100
context: Section 2.11.1.1 WHODAS 2.0 domains, scoring procedure, and key features
evidence_wording: The WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHO-DAS 2.0) is the internationally, culturally and socioeconomically validated generic functioning assessment instrument for an adult population. WHO DAS 2.0 is focused on ICF Activity and Participation domains and allows to compute an overall and domain specific functioning score covering the following domains: Cognition, Mobility, Self-care, Getting along, Life activities, Participation. Scoring has three steps: Step 1 - Summing recoded item scores within each domain; Step 2 - Summing all six domain scores; Step 3 - Converting summary score into 0 to 100 metric.

title: WHODAS 2.0 representation and coding structure (VD-codes)
subject: WHODAS 2.0 ICD-11 coding structure
object: alphanumeric codes starting with 'VD' and Foundation URIs to items, with response scale values and ICF category mappings
context: Section 2.11.1.2 and Table 1 (example WHODAS 2.0 item)
evidence_wording: To enable easy information retrieval each WHO DAS 2.0 item has an assigned alphanumeric code to represent the captured concepts of the respective item. The code starts with the letters 'VD' followed by a randomly assign number. Additional item specific information and values (i.e. item question, five-point response scale) are included in the ICD-11 APIs to allow for easy integration of the instrument and the automated scoring computation in any software application. Six domains are represented as block headings with URIs.

title: Generic functioning entities and VV coding structure
subject: Generic functioning entities
object: a functioning category and qualifier coded with prefix 'VV' and linked through postcoordination based on ICF generic core set
context: Sections 2.11.2, 2.11.2.1, and 2.11.2.2 Generic functioning entity features and representation
evidence_wording: The main tool for documenting functioning is a list of generic functioning domains derived from the ICF Annex 9 and the ICF generic core set. The generic list allows clinicians to generate a coded functioning profile of an individual which can be used for multiple purposes like goal setting, monitoring change, and communicating across care. In accordance with the WHO FIC content model a functioning entity has two components i.e. category and a qualifier. Both have an assigned alphanumeric code and an URI. The code starts with the letters 'VV' followed by a randomly assign number. Linked through postcoordination.

title: Electronic recording and reporting principles
subject: Electronic health documentation in ICD-11
object: lossless recording containing clinician verbatim text, Foundation URI, and ICD-11 code via API tools without artificial prompt restrictions
context: Section 2.12 Electronic recording and reporting best practice requirements
evidence_wording: Electronic documentation will follow the principle of lossless collection of information at the source. Best practice includes reporting of: 1. A text field that captures the clinical term or cause of death with the exact wording reported by the health provider, and 2. A data field that retains the identifier (URI) of the chosen entity of ICD-11 that represents the most exact match for that text. 3. A data field for the relevant ICD-11 code. Coding shall be done using tools based on the ICD-11 API. Software must not include lists or other prompts to guide the recording or coding.

title: Foundation Component architecture and Tabular lists generation
subject: ICD-11 Foundation Component
object: all linearizations and congruent tabular lists (MMS, PCL, VA, SMoL) with mono-hierarchical categories and multiple-parenting views
context: Section 2.13 Foundation Component and Tabular lists relationship
evidence_wording: The Foundation Component is a multi-dimensional collection of all ICD entities. ... Foundation Component also has the necessary information to use the entities to build a tabular list. Drawing on the same Foundation Component, a set of tabular lists that builds on the same hierarchical tree structure can be created - producing congruent tabular lists. Core tabular lists for international use: Mortality and Morbidity Statistics (MMS), Primary care low resources settings (PCL), Verbal Autopsy (VA), Startup Mortality List (SMoL). In a Tabular list, entities of Foundation become categories: mutually exclusive, jointly exhaustive, single parent.

title: Main uses of the ICD - Mortality statistics governance and comparability
subject: Mortality statistics instructions
object: internationally standardized data collection and coding rules adopted by the World Health Assembly to guarantee global health data comparability
context: Sections 2.14 and 2.15 Main uses of ICD for mortality and public health objectives
evidence_wording: This section concerns the rules and guidelines adopted by the World Health Assembly regarding the selection of a single cause or condition for routine tabulation from death certificates. Guidelines are also provided for the application of the rules and for coding of the condition selected for tabulation. ... It is of utmost importance that production of mortality data follows the procedures detailed next, since any deviation from the international instructions will impair international comparability. ... Individual countries should not correct what is assumed to be an error.

title: Definition of Underlying Cause of Death (UCOD)
subject: Underlying cause of death (UCOD)
object: (a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced fatal injury
context: Section 2.15.1 Underlying cause of death statutory definition
evidence_wording: Effective public health interventions prevent harm or death by breaking the chain of events that lead to harm. For this purpose, the underlying cause of death has been defined as '(a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced the fatal injury', and is selected for routine single-cause tabulation of mortality statistics.

title: Data source - The international form of Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD)
subject: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Frame A)
object: Part 1 for sequence of events directly leading to death and Part 2 for other significant contributing conditions
context: Section 2.15.2 Structure and certification requirements of the international MCCD form
evidence_wording: The international mortality coding instructions presuppose that data have been collected with a death certificate conforming to the international form of Medical Certificate of Cause of Death as recommended by the WHO. Frame A, the medical data part of the international form is split into two parts: Part 1 is for diseases related to the chain of events directly leading to death, and Part 2 is for other significant conditions contributing to death. ... It is the responsibility of the medical practitioner or other qualified certifier ... to use clinical judgment.

title: Routine cause of death reporting systems and Verbal autopsy (VA)
subject: Routine death registration and verbal autopsy
object: causes of death in formal healthcare settings and community settings lacking medical certification, respectively
context: Sections 2.15.3, 2.15.3.1 Routine systems, and 2.15.3.2 Verbal autopsy
evidence_wording: In routine cause of death reporting systems, every individual death is certified by a qualified medical doctor who carries out an accurate postmortem examination, collects history from relatives, and has access to all pre-existing medical information. ... Verbal autopsy (VA) is a method used to ascertain the cause of a death based on an interview with next of kin or other caregivers where no medical certification is available. This is done using a standardised instrument that elicits information on signs, symptoms, medical history, and circumstances preceding death.

title: Basic mortality concepts - Terminal cause of death
subject: Terminal cause of death (immediate cause of death)
object: the condition entered first on the first used line of Part 1 of the death certificate
context: Section 2.16 Basic concepts and 2.16.1 Terminal cause of death
evidence_wording: The disease or condition entered first on the first used line of Part 1 of the death certificate is the cause directly leading to death. This is known as the terminal or immediate cause of death. Example: 1 (a) Myocardial infarction due to (b) Coronary atherosclerosis -> Myocardial infarction is the terminal cause of death.

title: Basic mortality concepts - Causal relationship and sequence
subject: Causal relationship and sequence in mortality coding
object: a chain or series of medical events where each condition is a complication of or caused by the previous step, evaluated on medical and epidemiological criteria
context: Section 2.16.2 Causal relationship and sequence definition and rules
evidence_wording: A causal relationship exists if a condition mentioned on the death certificate can be caused by another condition also mentioned on the certificate. The term 'sequence' refers to a chain or series of medical events in which each step is a complication of, or is caused by, the previous step. A causal relationship can exist between any two conditions, including conditions assigned to the same ICD-11 code, regardless of where each condition was reported. In a correctly completed death certificate, a sequence is a set of conditions reported line by line with a causal relationship between each element. Four lines are provided in Part 1.

title: Basic mortality concepts - Starting point and Tentative Starting Point (TSP)
subject: Starting point of causal sequence
object: the condition or event that started the sequence of acceptable causal relationships ending with the terminal cause of death
context: Section 2.16.3 Starting point definition and sequential TSP identification
evidence_wording: The starting point is the condition or event that started the sequence of acceptable causal relationships ending with the terminal cause of death. In a correctly completed death certificate, the condition reported first on the lowest used line in Part 1 is the starting point of the sequence. The instructions on how to identify the starting point is provided in Section 2.17.3 Find the starting point (Steps SP1 to SP8). ... The condition provisionally considered as the starting point when applying the instructions step by step is referred to as the 'tentative starting point (TSP)' and may change several times.

title: Basic mortality concepts - Duration
subject: Duration of disease or condition on death certificate
object: the interval from onset of the disease or condition to the time of death
context: Section 2.16.4 Duration definition
evidence_wording: On death certificates, each reported condition should also include information about duration. The duration refers to the interval from the onset of the disease or condition to the time of death. Note that it is not always the same as the time of diagnosis of the condition, which may be at the same time as, or after, the onset of symptoms.

title: Basic mortality concepts - First-mentioned sequence identification
subject: First-mentioned sequence in Part 1
object: tracing from terminal cause of death on the top line downwards, evaluating conditions on lower lines from left to right to establish causal connections
context: Section 2.16.5 First-mentioned sequence tracing protocol
evidence_wording: A death certificate may contain several sequences of acceptable causal relationships ending with the terminal cause of death. The coding instructions are given to identify the starting point of the first-mentioned sequence in Part 1 (See also Step SP4). ... To identify the first-mentioned sequence, begin with the terminal cause of death (the condition entered first on the first used line of Part 1). Check if the conditions on the next line in Part 1 can result in the terminal cause of death. If several conditions are reported on the same line, check from left to right in turn until you find a condition that could cause the terminal cause. ... Continue until you have found a condition that can cause the tentative starting point.

title: Congenital or constitutional haemorrhagic condition due to other conditions
subject: congenital or constitutional haemorrhagic condition (3B10-3B1Z)
predicate: do not accept as due to
object: any other cause
context: Step SP3/SP4 accepted and rejected sequences
evidence_wording: Do not accept congenital or constitutional haemorrhagic condition 3B10-3B1Z as due to any other cause.

title: Anaphylaxis due to external causes
subject: Anaphylaxis (4A84)
predicate: do not accept as due to any other causes except
object: Intentional self-harm (PB80-PD3Z) or Assault (PD50-PF2Z)
context: Step SP3/SP4; accompanying Consequence/Caused-by table on printed 100
exception_condition: accept Intentional self-harm or Assault; do not accept other causes
evidence_wording: Do not accept Anaphylaxis (4A84) as due to any other causes except Intentional self-harm (PB80-PD3Z) or Assault (PD50-PF2Z).
